The UI must start as root. It uses the installed venv, then delegates database operations through a private pipe to a worker under `paperang-relay`. This keeps SQLite/WAL ownership compatible with the live service. The local root actor is written to audit events, never inserted as a credential or user. The console creates no persistent daemon. Receivers use scoped M keys; C administration is available in native clients. Public submissions require a registered browser identity; Explicit A keys cannot read print status; anonymous browser identities and B can read only their own states. Task content is available only in C history or a matching device-scoped active claim (M or proven public-key C).

Initial C/M/B credentials are written once to `/var/lib/paperang-relay/initial-credentials.jsonl` with root-only permissions. Keep M in the receiving client and C only for management. Existing configs and credentials are preserved. Only POST `/v2/jobs` accepts up to **160 KiB (163840 bytes)** JSON; all other JSON requests remain 64 KiB. The largest raw raster is 100800 bytes, base64 134400 characters. Ensure reverse proxy body limits allow at least 160 KiB. The bounded JSON envelope avoids multipart uploads and a second upload lifecycle for these small print-ready bitmaps. Base64 has 33% wire overhead, but one-bit raster is 1/24 of RGB before that overhead (a 576×384 image is 27648 bytes raw).

The owner explicitly requires retiring Mac local HTTP API v1 in this patch baseline. This compatibility exception returns 410, requires local callers to migrate to v2 and stable English job states, and does not change Relay v2, template/content schema 1 or physical protocol. The numeric baseline identifies one product generation and its compatibility contract. Matching baselines mean the declared shared relay API, content and template schemas interoperate, with equivalent semantics for implemented common features. It does not mean a relay server has a printer UI or a tray-only client has every full-client tool. Scope differences must be explicit in the matrix; an unimplemented mandatory feature blocks a full-client parity claim.
- **MAJOR** changes for a breaking shared contract or incompatible product generation.
- **PATCH** changes for a shared baseline correction requiring coordination across distributions, even if backward compatible.

- **`fixN`** identifies a distribution-only compatible correction or local improvement. Counters are local to each baseline/distribution and restart when the baseline changes. Never change API/schema semantics incompatibly under a fix note.
